admissionTopologies.derivation: Derived only from PROPOSED-RULES.md section 1. Proposed in repair2 and accepted by root as written (OPEN-QUESTIONS.json OQ-06, decision A). The original sha1 literal repository is a primary repository whose .git is a directory and therefore has no marker, gitdir or commondir file. Repair3 checked this against the now in-packet fixture construction evidence: fixtures/manifest.json command sha1-init runs git init on repositories/sha1, and its recorded stdout names repositories/sha1/.git/ (inherited/fixtures/FIXTURES.pack.json). This is construction evidence, not a runtime observation. The expected result of every case is unchanged.
admissionTopologies.notation: B is the single pinned absolute, lexically clean qualification base directory (PROPOSED-RULES.md section 6). It consists only of ordinary directories, and its UTF-8 spelling contains no NUL, CR, LF or 0xFF byte. R, G, A and W denote the UTF-8 bytes of absolute, lexically clean paths. + is byte concatenation. Quoted byte strings use JSON escapes. Any byte that is not printable ASCII is named in hex.

T-LINKED.purpose: Minimal reciprocal linked worktree over the unchanged original ordinary-sha1 repository. It is required because a primary .git directory has no regular marker, gitdir backpointer or commondir file into which bytes or errors could be injected.
directories: R = B + "/repo": the original ordinary-sha1 literal repository with its .git directory, byte-unchanged. G = R + "/.git" is the primary .git directory and its own common directory.
A = G + "/worktrees/wt": a new ordinary directory (G/worktrees is also new), mode 0755. This is the per-worktree administrative directory.
W = B + "/wt": a new ordinary directory, mode 0755. W is the repository path given to the verifier. It needs no checked-out files.

files.bytes: "../..\n" (resolved against A and lexically cleaned, this selects G)

mustNotExist: any alternates, http-alternates or attributes entry not already present in the original fixture
T-LINKED.notInspected: Admission does not read A/HEAD, A/index or any other Git per-worktree file, and they are not required, because every T-LINKED case refuses before any Git transaction. A harness may create them, for example with git worktree add --detach. If it does, it must then overwrite W/.git, A/gitdir and A/commondir with exactly the bytes above.
T-LINKED.control: With no injection, T-LINKED must pass every metadata admission step of PROPOSED-RULES.md section 1: root, marker, administrative directory, backpointer and reciprocity, commondir and common directory, and objects topology. This control establishes the recipes' statement that all earlier ordered metadata entries succeed. It is not a new full-result case.

cases.recipe: Topology T-LINKED (/admissionTopologies). The verifier repository path is W. Inject exactly: replace the root marker W + "/.git" with a regular file of mode 0644 and exactly 4097 bytes, "gitdir: " + A + Q + "\n". Let n = 4088 - len(A), which must be at least 0. Q is n/2 copies of "/." when n is even. When n is odd, Q is one "/" followed by (n-1)/2 copies of "/.". Lexical cleaning of A + Q yields A, so only the inclusive 4,096-byte bound is violated, and the refusal occurs at the bounded read before any path resolution. Original ordinary-sha1 literal map, config, artifacts and base/target inputs are otherwise unchanged. All earlier ordered metadata entries succeed. No content transaction or evidence progress.

cases.recipe: After the exact target sidecar is committed, the canonical diff transaction reaches its per-operation deadline (controlled monotonic clock; numeric spans belong to the implementing Gate A timing ledger, OQ-05 B). Ordinary abnormal teardown of the proven owned group starts at once with zero TERM grace. Commitment point: the transaction returns its git-timeout failure to the repository verifier stage first. The outer 30-minute span then expires while that ordinary abnormal teardown is still in progress. This starts the single emergency 10-second retirement allowance, anchored to the expiry, with no new Git work. Teardown completes within it and is observed. The returned failure stands (OQ-04 C): the result is identical to canonical-per-op-timeout. Patch digest remains null. Failed or unobserved teardown would instead be repository/unsupported-process-containment, as in outer-expiry-content-unobserved.
